title: Same Document. Different Chunkers. Different Recall.

intro.before: A retriever can only return the chunks you gave it. Where you cut the text decides

bullets.text: Splits every N tokens, overlapping the edges
Simple, fast and predictable chunk sizes
Overlap keeps facts that sit on a boundary
Cuts through sentences, tables and code
Tries paragraphs, then lines, then words
Keeps paragraphs whole when they fit
A solid default for mixed prose
Still size-driven, not meaning-driven
Splits on Markdown or HTML headings
Keeps tables and code blocks intact
Adds the heading path as chunk metadata
Needs clean, well-structured source docs
Embeds sentences, splits where meaning jumps
Chunks follow topics, not character counts
Fewer mixed-topic chunks in the index
An embedding call per sentence to index
Encodes the whole document in one pass
Pools token vectors per chunk afterwards
Chunk vectors keep document-wide context
Needs a long-context embedding model
LLM rewrites text into standalone facts
Resolves pronouns so each fact stands alone
Precise matches for fact-lookup questions
An LLM call per passage; slow to index

principles.sub: Measure retrieval recall before paying for semantic or LLM-based chunking.
Chunk one corpus several ways; compare how often the right passage lands in the top k.
Store the heading path as metadata or prepend it to the chunk text.

rows.q: Long docs that drift across topics

quote.big: A retriever can't find what you cut apart.
quote.small: Chunking sets the ceiling for recall.
